StartLux-Decision is a family of open decision models. Given a state (text, JSON or images) and a set of typed
questions, a model returns a probability for every option of every question: a choice among listed options
(`choice`), a yes or no judgement (`noul`), or a level on a scale (`score`). Instant models answer in a single forward
pass with bidirectional attention over the prompt. AutoThink models answer in one pass when the top probability
reaches a gate, 0.6 by default, and otherwise generate a short reasoning trace and read the answer again.

This repository contains the inference engine and HTTP server for both variants. The API is compatible with System
One `/v1/systemone`.

<p align="center"><img src="docs/assets/score_vs_size.png" width="860" alt="Decision Index 0.3 public score against model size"></p>

In the chess and game runs, every step is one request with typed questions, answered by StartLux-Decision-v1-27B, the
first release, in one pass. The rescue and launch videos send one frame a second with nine questions to the 27B
AutoThink model on [bamboonode.dev](https://bamboonode.dev/), which thinks only when its top probability is below the
0.6 gate. Their footage is from the U.S. Coast Guard and NASA (public domain, no endorsement implied), and the faces of
the people being rescued are blurred. Click a preview for the video. [v1/README.md](v1/README.md#demos) describes each
harness, and the harnesses for computer use and chess are in [v1/demos](v1/demos).

## Release notes

- 2026-10-16: StartLux-Decision v1.1 27B Instant ranks first of 174 entries on the
  [Decision Index 0.3.2](https://huggingface.co/spaces/multimodalart/jev-decision-index) leaderboard on Hugging Face,
  with a Full score of 69.12. It is also first on each of the three parts: the public benchmarks (72.88), the private
  tests of the same skills (64.82) and the private tasks from new domains (61.41).
- 2026-10: the technical report is on arXiv as [2610.17309](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17309).

Decision Index 0.3 refers to the public subset, evaluated with the public kit. DecisionPivot reports pair accuracy on
7,800 programmatically generated examples arranged in contrast pairs that differ in one decisive detail. A pair counts
only when both answers are correct. The AutoThink results use a gate of 0.9.

Across sizes, the Instant models exceed the strongest evaluated decision model of comparable size by 7.4 to 16.9 points
on Decision Index 0.3, and AutoThink adds 11.5 to 18.4 points of DecisionPivot pair accuracy over Instant. AutoThink
reasoning is trained with RLCDÂ², reinforcement learning for calibrated deliberative decisions. The technical report
contains the full evaluation. The engine also serves the
[v1 models](https://huggingface.co/collections/startlux-models/startlux-decision-v1-6abba92b301b573fa154d493)
(0.8B to 27B and 35B-A3B), which answer in one pass.

On one H200 with vLLM and one request in flight, Instant models answer a request in 25 to 52 ms at the median, from
0.8B to 27B. Through this server, an AutoThink model needs one read-out of 38 to 59 ms when it is sure. When it is
unsure it writes a thought and reads the answer a second time, and the thought takes longer the more it writes.

## Quick start

To try a model without a GPU, use [bamboonode.dev](https://bamboonode.dev/). It hosts the 27B AutoThink model with the
same request format (`POST /v1/decisions`), free and without usage limits, and needs only a Bamboo API key.

To run the models yourself, install the package into the same Python environment as vLLM. It carries the vLLM plugin
that Instant models need.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/StartLux-Decision.git
cd StartLux-Decision
pip install -e '.[vllm]'          # vLLM 0.31.0; the published numbers were measured on 0.19.1, which is also supported
```

Download a model and start one vLLM server per GPU with the decision server in front of them:

```bash
hf download startlux-models/StartLux-Decision-v1.1-4B-AutoThink --local-dir models/StartLux-Decision-v1.1-4B-AutoThink
startlux-decide serve --model models/StartLux-Decision-v1.1-4B-AutoThink --launch-vllm --gpus 0,1,2,3 --port 8090
```

Ask a question:

```bash
curl -s localhost:8090/v1/systemone -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "state": {"ticket": "I was charged twice for order #4411 and the app still shows it as unpaid."},
  "questions": {
    "team":     {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which team should handle this ticket?",
                 "criteria": {"billing": "Payments and refunds", "shipping": "Delivery", "technical": "App and login"}},
    "urgent":   {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Should this ticket be answered today?"},
    "severity": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How severe is the impact?",
                 "criteria": ["cosmetic", "annoying", "blocks the customer"]}
  }
}'
```

The 27B AutoThink model answers (numbers rounded):

```json
{"answers": {
  "team":     {"type": "choice", "choice": "billing", "confidence": 0.992,
               "probabilities": {"billing": 0.995, "shipping": 0.000, "technical": 0.005},
               "none_probability": 0.002},
  "urgent":   {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.870},
  "severity": {"type": "score", "score": 1.858, "confidence": 0.787,
               "legend": {"0": "cosmetic", "1": "annoying", "2": "blocks the customer"},
               "probabilities": {"0": 0.005, "1": 0.133, "2": 0.863}}},
 "usage": {"input_tokens": 290, "output_tokens": 144}, "model": "startlux-decision-27b-autothink"}
```

`noul` is the probability of yes. `score` is the expected level, with a probability for every level.
`none_probability` is the chance that none of the listed options fits (see Controls).

[examples/](examples) has the same request in Python, a request with an image and a small batch client.

## Controls

A request can steer the reasoning of AutoThink models and ask for more detail. All fields are optional.

| Field | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `think_mode` | `auto` | `auto` reasons when the first read-out's top probability is below `gate`; `never` answers in one pass; `always` reasons first |
| `gate` | 0.6 | the confidence below which `auto` reasons (the published results use 0.9) |
| `think_budget` | 4096 | the longest thought, in tokens |
| `none_check` | true | every choice answer reports `none_probability`, the chance that no listed option fits; `choice` stays a listed option |
| `allow_none` | false (`serve --allow-none`: true) | lets `choice` be null when "None of the above" is the most likely answer |
| `return_details`, `return_thought` | false | per-answer read-outs and timings, and the thought text |
| `images` | none | base64 strings or data URIs used as evidence |

The default gate of 0.6 answers more requests in one pass. A gate of 0.9 thinks more often and is more accurate on
decisions that need rules or arithmetic. For the 27B AutoThink model on this engine, moving the gate from 0.9 to 0.6
lowers Decision Index 0.3 from 73.22 to 72.85 and DecisionPivot pair accuracy from 88.1% to 68.4%. Instant models
always answer in one pass.

We suggest treating a `none_probability` of 0.2 or more as "no listed option fits". At 0.2 it catches two thirds
(66.3%) of the questions whose listed options are all wrong, and flags 2.2% of the questions that do have a right
answer. Lower thresholds flag many more good questions, higher ones miss more of the bad ones
([why 0.2](docs/none_probability.md#why-02)). [docs/api.md](docs/api.md) describes the full request and response
format, the confidence definitions, the details fields and the errors.

## Engines

| Engine | Instant | AutoThink | Images | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM (default) | yes, with the plugin in this package | yes | vLLM 0.31 | serving, and the published numbers |
| llama.cpp | yes, GGUF builds marked non-causal | yes | with the `mmproj` file | machines without vLLM |
| MLX | yes, mlx-vlm builds | yes | yes | Apple Silicon |
| transformers | yes | yes | yes | reference checks |

FP8 and GGUF Q8_0 largely preserve BF16 decision performance, while Q4_K_M can lose up to 4.3 points (27B AutoThink
on DecisionPivot). [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md)
lists the engine settings to switch on and off and why, and [docs/quantization.md](docs/quantization.md) covers the
quantized builds.

## Serving in production

`startlux-decide serve` can face the internet directly, with API keys, HTTPS, early 429 responses under load, an
access log and an optional request log. [docs/serving_publicly.md](docs/serving_publicly.md) has a complete command
and a checklist. The other commands measure a deployment: `bench` for latency, `eval` for accuracy and calibration on
labelled requests, and `quantize` for FP8, GGUF and MLX builds.

## Tests

```bash
python -m unittest -v
```

The tests need only the standard library and skip the parts that need aiohttp, torch or transformers when those are
missing. Set `STARTLUX_TEST_MODEL_DIR` to a model folder to add checks against its real tokenizer.

## The first release

StartLux-Decision-v1 (0.8B to 27B and a 35B-A3B mixture of experts) answers every question in one pass. Its inference
code, evaluation scripts, results, game logs and demo harnesses are in [v1/](v1), and the repository as it was at that
release is tagged `v1`. The engine in this repository serves the v1 models as well.

FILE: CHANGELOG.md

# Changelog

## 1.1.0 (unreleased)

First public release of the engine, for the StartLux-Decision v1.1 models (Instant and AutoThink) and the earlier v1
models.

- Decision server with the `/v1/systemone` request format (also served as `/v1/decisions`), typed questions
  (`choice`, `noul`, `score`) and a probability for every option.
- AutoThink path: confidence gate, thought generation with a loop check, second read-out and mixture, with request
  controls `think_mode`, `gate`, `think_budget` and `mix`.
- `allow_none`: an opt-in "None of the above" option for choice questions, with `none_probability` in the answer.
- Default gate 0.6, so that more requests are answered in one pass. The published numbers used 0.9 (`--gate 0.9`).
- Engines: vLLM 0.19.1 and 0.31 (with a plugin for prompt-bidirectional Instant models), transformers, llama.cpp
  (GGUF, with patches for Instant models) and MLX (mlx-vlm).
- The `vllm` extra installs vLLM 0.31.0, which fixes the security advisories against 0.19.1. The engine still runs
  on 0.19.1, the version of the published numbers.
- Images in the evidence and prompts up to 262,144 tokens.
- Production serving: API keys, TLS, early 429 responses, an access log and an optional request log.
- Tools: `launch-vllm`, `bench`, `eval` and `quantize` (FP8, GGUF and MLX builds).
- Choice options given as a list, or under `options`, are knocked out like `{option: description}`. Before, a list of
  more than 26 options, or of 26 when the extra "None of the above" option was added (`none_check` is on by default),
  was refused with a 422.

# Contributing

Bug reports, fixes and documentation improvements are welcome.

Before you open a pull request, run the unit tests with `python -m unittest -v`. They need only the standard library
and skip the parts that need aiohttp, numpy, torch, transformers or mlx-vlm when those are missing. A change to the
prompts, the read-out or the AutoThink path must keep the probabilities of the golden test (`tests/test_golden.py`)
identical, or explain in the pull request why and by how much they move. A change that affects accuracy or latency
should come with numbers measured with `startlux-decide eval` or `startlux-decide bench` on the same hardware before
and after.

Keep the code in the style of the surrounding files and keep new dependencies optional where possible. By contributing
you agree that your contribution is licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

# Security

Please report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub's
[private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/StartLux-Decision/security/advisories/new) and not in
a public issue. Include the version or commit, the command line of the server and the smallest request that shows
the problem. We will acknowledge the report and keep you informed while we work on a fix.

The server is built to face the internet only with API keys, TLS and request limits switched on; see
[docs/serving_publicly.md](docs/serving_publicly.md). The vLLM servers it launches listen on 127.0.0.1 and have no
authentication of their own, so never expose their ports.

FILE: docs/api.md

# API

The server speaks the TypeSafe `/v1/systemone` format, so TypeSafe clients work against it. `POST /v1/decisions` is the
same API under OpenRouter's name. Every question of a request runs as its own task: a question that thinks does not hold
up the others, and many requests can be in flight. Serving publicly (API keys, HTTPS, early 429s, the OpenRouter models
document, the access log): [serving_publicly.md](serving_publicly.md).

## POST /v1/systemone (and /v1/decisions)

### Request

```json
{
  "state": "any text, or any JSON value",
  "questions": {
    "team":     {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which team?", "criteria": {"billing": "Payments", "shipping": null}},
    "urgent":   {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Answer today?"},
    "severity": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How bad?", "criteria": ["minor", "major", "critical"]}
  },
  "images": ["data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQ..."],
  "think_mode": "auto", "gate": 0.6, "think_budget": 4096, "mix": 0.75, "thought_generation": "auto",
  "allow_none": false, "none_check": true, "return_details": false, "return_thought": false
}
```

| question type | criteria | answer |
|---|---|---|
| `choice` | `{option id: description or null}`, or a list of option ids | `choice`, `confidence`, `probabilities` over every option |
| `noul` (yes/no; `bool` is accepted) | optional `{"true": description, "false": description}` | `noul`: the probability of yes |
| `score` | a list of 2 to 10 levels, lowest first, or `{key: level}` with numeric keys (sorted ascending) | `score` (probability-weighted mean level), `confidence`, `legend`, `probabilities` keyed `"0"` to `"n-1"` |

`instructions` is required for choice and score questions; a yes/no question without it asks "Which answer fits the
evidence?". A JSON state is rendered as compact JSON; arrays of 8 or more elements carry an `_index` on each element.

Images (optional, as in v1): `images` is a list of base64 strings or data URIs. In the state, `<image>` marks where
each image goes, one mark per image, in order (a JSON state may hold the marks in its strings). Without marks the
images come first (`Image 1:`, `Image 2:` ... on their own lines when there are several), then a blank line and the
state. Each image is resized to at most 1,048,576 pixels and at least 65,536, keeping its aspect ratio, with both
sides multiples of 32 pixels, and becomes one token per 32 Ã— 32 pixels (a 1024 Ã— 1024 photo is 1,024 tokens). Every
question of the request reads every image, and `usage.input_tokens` counts the image tokens. At most 8 images per
request by default (`serve --max-images`, `--max-pixels`; `--no-images` serves text only). Images need a folder with
a vision tower and an engine that reads them: vLLM 0.31 or later, transformers, llama.cpp when llama-server has an
mmproj file ([engines.md](engines.md#llamacpp)), or MLX with an mlx-vlm folder. Any other engine answers 422.

Long states: a prompt can be as long as the engine's context. On vLLM 0.31 that is 262,144 tokens (the models' native
context) for AutoThink and v1 folders and 131,072 tokens for Instant folders, unless the server was started with a
lower `--max-model-len`. A longer prompt gets a 422 with the engine's reason. AutoThink and v1 folders read a long
state shared by the questions of a request once; an Instant folder reads it again for every question, because it
reads each prompt bidirectionally.

Choice lists: one pass reads up to 26 options (letters A to Z). A list of more options is knocked out: near-equal
groups of at most 25 are read in one pass each, the 3 best of every group go to a final round (the 26 best overall when
more than 26 qualify), and the options that miss the final share 0.001 of the probability in proportion to their group
round. The final round is an ordinary question (it may think). A choice with a single option is answered without the
model (probability 1).

None of the above (`choice` questions only). `serve` checks every choice question for a missing answer by default
(`none_check`): the question gets one extra last option, "None of the above", the answer carries `none_probability`,
and `choice` stays the most likely listed option. On 51,506 benchmark questions this left accuracy unchanged (84.66 with
and without it, thinking on). `"none_check": false` in a request, or `serve --no-none-check`, turns it off. With
`"allow_none": true` (opt-in) a choice question also gets one extra last
option, "None of the above", shown to the model like any other option (and visible to the thought, which can choose
it); the read-out covers n + 1 options. The answer then has `choice` null when that option is the most likely one (a tie
goes to the listed option), `probabilities` over your options only, renormalised to sum to 1 (a client that ignores the
new field sees an ordinary distribution), and `none_probability`, the probability of the extra option before the
renormalisation. `confidence` is computed as usual from the renormalised probabilities, so it describes the spread
over your options, and `none_probability` is the signal to act on. A choice with a single option is read by the model
when `allow_none` is on (two options), not answered at once. In a knocked-out list the extra option is added in the
final round only, and a list of 26 options is knocked out too (the 26th letter is the extra option). An option of your
own called "None of the above" gets a 422. With `allow_none` off, which is the default unless the server runs with `--allow-none`, nothing changes: the prompts,
answers and scores are exactly those without the control. `allow_none` can also be set on one question
(`{"type": "choice", ..., "allow_none": true}`), which overrides the request; `null` means not given. Other question
types ignore it.

Reading `none_probability`: it is an alarm score, not a calibrated probability, and 0.2 is the threshold we suggest.
On 51,506 choice questions of DecisionPivot and Decision Index 0.3 (27B AutoThink, thinking on), each asked as
published and once more with its right option removed, a threshold of 0.2 caught 66.3% of the questions without a
right option and flagged 2.2% of the published ones (AUROC 0.920). [none_probability.md](none_probability.md) has the
other thresholds, why 0.2, the tasks where it is not reliable and how it interacts with thinking. `confidence` alone
separates the two kinds of question much worse, because hard questions with a right option also read low. The extra
option also gives a thought a way out: without it, a question that has no fitting option often makes the thought go
round in circles until the budget, since the model must still pick a listed option.

`confidence` follows TypeSafe: for a choice (p_max âˆ’ 1/n) / (1 âˆ’ 1/n), clamped to [0, 1]; for a score 1 minus the
probability-weighted distance in levels from the most likely level, divided by the same distance for an even spread
measured from the middle level, floored at 0. Yes/no answers have no confidence; |2p âˆ’ 1| is the equivalent.

### Controls

| field | values | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `think_mode` | `auto` / `never` / `always` (also `hybrid` / `plain` / `think`) | `auto`: think when the first read-out's top probability is below `gate` |
| `gate` | number in [0, 1] | the threshold of `auto` |
| `think_budget` | integer â‰¥ 1 | most thought tokens; larger values are capped by the server's maximum (`serve --max-think-budget`, default: the default budget) |
| `mix` | number in [0, 1] | final = (1 âˆ’ mix) Â· first read-out + mix Â· read-out after the thought; 0 ignores the thought, 1 uses only the read-out after it |
| `thought_generation` | `auto` / `stream` / `chunked` | how a thought is generated. `stream`: one streamed request; the loop detector looks at the thought each time another 1,024 tokens have arrived and ends the request when it loops. `chunked`: requests of 1,024 tokens, each re-sending the prompt and the thought so far, with the loop detector between them. `auto`: `stream` when the engine streams thoughts (vLLM 0.31 or later), else `chunked`. `stream` on another engine gets a 422 |
| `allow_none` | bool, default false (true with `serve --allow-none`) | choice questions get the extra last option "None of the above" (see above); a question's own `allow_none` overrides it; ignored by `noul` and `score` questions; a non-boolean gets a 422 |
| `none_check` | bool, default true in `serve` | choice questions get the extra option internally and report `none_probability`; `choice` stays a listed option unless `allow_none` is set; a non-boolean gets a 422 |
| `return_details` | bool | adds `details` to every answer and `timing_ms` to the response |
| `return_thought` | bool | also returns the thought text; implies `return_details` |

A missing or null field takes the server default. The server defaults are the model folder's (built-in AutoThink
defaults, or an `auto_think` block in its `decision_config.json`; v1 folders answer in one pass, `never`), then the
`serve` options. Instant models never think:
`think_mode` `auto` or `always` gets a 422; `gate`, `mix` and `think_budget` are accepted and have no effect. A thought
also needs room in the engine's context: the budget is cut to the context length minus the prompt minus 64 tokens, and
when that leaves 32 tokens or fewer the question is answered from the first read-out.

Long thoughts: a thought that runs to the budget is the slowest part of a request. One thought is generated at about
27 tokens/s on an A800 in BF16, so 4,096 tokens take about 150 s. `details.thought.ended` is `budget` for such a thought.
On the 10,000 questions above, 4% of the questions ran to the budget and used over a third of all thought tokens. Most
were hard questions, where the long thought still pays (38% answered right against 22% from the first read-out
alone). Questions without a fitting option run to the budget more often (5.9% against 3.9% with `allow_none` on), and
there the long thought gains nothing. Three things keep thoughts short on such questions. Ask
only the questions that apply to the current step (an agent that has decided to scroll should not also ask which link
to click). Add options such as "not visible" or "other" where the case may fall outside the list. Turn on `allow_none`
where the list may be incomplete. Lowering `think_budget` makes every hard question pay: on DecideBench the 27B
AutoThink model scores 88.6 with 4,096 tokens, 80.4 with 512 and 68.4 with 256, against about 70 when it answers in one
pass (`never`).

### Response

```json
{
  "answers": {
    "team": {"type": "choice", "choice": "billing", "confidence": 0.81, "probabilities": {"billing": 0.905, "shipping": 0.095}},
    "urgent": {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.64},
    "severity": {"type": "score", "score": 1.3, "confidence": 0.19, "legend": {"0": "minor", "1": "major", "2": "critical"},
                 "probabilities": {"0": 0.12, "1": 0.46, "2": 0.42}}
  },
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 290, "output_tokens": 0},
  "model": "StartLux-Decision-4B"
}
```

With `allow_none` a choice answer also carries `none_probability` and may have `"choice": null`:

```json
"team": {"type": "choice", "choice": null, "confidence": 0.33, "probabilities": {"billing": 0.667, "shipping": 0.333},
         "none_probability": 0.7}
```

`usage.input_tokens` counts the tokens of every one-pass prompt read (all rounds of a knocked-out list);
`usage.output_tokens` counts thought tokens.

### Details and timings

With `return_details`, every answer carries:

```json
"details": {
  "first_pass":    {"probabilities": {"billing": 0.55, "shipping": 0.45}, "top": 0.55, "ms": 21.4},
  "thought":       {"used": true, "tokens": 812, "ended": "closed", "ms": 2140.7, "generation": "stream",
                    "text": "Let me work through ..."},
  "after_thought": {"probabilities": {"billing": 0.97, "shipping": 0.03}, "ms": 24.9},
  "gate": 0.6,
  "mix": 0.75,
  "total_ms": 2188.3
}
```

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `first_pass.probabilities` | the first read-out, keyed as the answer (after a knock-out: over every option); with `allow_none` it also has the key `None of the above` and sums to 1 over all of them, as read (not renormalised) |
| `first_pass.top` | its top probability over the options read in the final pass: the value compared with the gate |
| `first_pass.ms` | time of the engine calls of the first pass (the knock-out rounds and the final read-out) |
| `thought.used`, `thought.tokens` | whether the question thought, and the thought tokens generated |
| `thought.ended` | `closed` (the model closed the thought), `loop` (the loop detector ended it), `budget` (cut: budget or context reached; the read-out then sees the line "I have to decide now with what I have worked out so far."), `skipped` (no thought) |
| `thought.ms` | from sending the thought request (the first chunk) to receiving its end (the last chunk; wave waits included) |
| `thought.generation` | `stream` or `chunked` (see the controls); only when the question thought |
| `thought.text` | with `return_thought`: the whole thought, forced start included; the read-out after it sees its last 4,000 characters |
| `after_thought` | the read-out after the thought, re-tempered, and the time of its engine call; null without a thought |
| `gate` | the gate the first read-out was compared with; null when it was not consulted (`never`, `always`, Instant, single-option lists) |
| `mix` | the mixture weight applied; null without a thought |
| `total_ms` | the question's whole pipeline |

The response also gets `timing_ms`: `wall` (the request inside the server, from validation to the answers),
`first_pass_sum` and `after_thought_sum` (sums over the questions of their read-out times; questions run concurrently,
so these can exceed `wall`), and `thought_span` (from the first thought's first chunk to the last thought's last
chunk; 0 without a thought).

### Errors

Every response carries `x-request-id` (the client's own when it sent a valid one, up to 128 characters of
`A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`) and the same value in `x-typesafe-request-id`. Errors are JSON:

```json
{"error": "gate must be a number from 0 to 1, not 2", "detail": [{"loc": ["body", "gate"], "msg": "...", "type": "value_error"}]}
```

| status | when |
|---|---|
| 401 | the server has API keys and the request has no `Authorization: Bearer <key>` with one of them (every route but `/health`) |
| 429 | the server is at `--max-inflight` decision requests; answered at once with `Retry-After: 1` |
| 422 | the body is not JSON or not an object; a control has a bad value (also `allow_none` that is not true or false, on the request or on a choice question); a question cannot be rendered (no instructions, 11 score levels, duplicate ids, ...); an Instant model is asked to think; `images` that cannot be read, more images than allowed, `<image>` marks that do not match the images, or images on an engine or folder that reads text only; the engine refuses a question (prompt longer than its context) |
| 404, 405 | unknown path or method |
| 502 | the engine failed or could not be reached (four tries per call) |

A 401 or 422 is final; a 429 or 502 may be retried. A `model` field in the request is accepted and ignored; the
response's `model` is the server's name.

## Model folders

A model folder holds the weights, the tokenizer, `config.json` and `decision_config.json`. The package reads:

| `decision_config.json` key | meaning |
|---|---|
| `temperature_by_type` | read-out temperature per question type (`choice`, `noul`, `score`; a missing type uses 1.0) |
| `letter_token_ids` | token ids of A to Z, checked against the tokenizer |
| `max_options_per_pass` | 26 (anything else is refused) |
| `wide_choice` | `{"group": 25, "keep": 3, "residual": 0.001}`: the knock-out of choice lists over 26 options |
| `prompt_attention` | `"bidirectional"` in Instant folders; must agree with `jev_prompt_attention` in `config.json` |
| `release_date` | reported by `/v1/models` (optional) |
| `auto_think` | optional, causal folders only: overrides of the AutoThink defaults below |

The folder's kind follows from `config.json`: `"jev_prompt_attention": "bidirectional"` is an Instant folder, anything
else is served as AutoThink. A causal folder trained for one pass only can carry `"auto_think": {"think_mode":
"never"}` (or be served with `--think-mode never`).

| `auto_think` key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `think_mode` | `"auto"` | default of the request field |
| `gate` | 0.6 | default of the request field (the published numbers used 0.9) |
| `mix` | 0.75 | default of the request field |
| `budget` | 4096 | default `think_budget` |
| `prefix` | `"Let me work through this carefully, step by step.\n"` | forced start of every thought |
| `tail_chars` | 4000 | the read-out after the thought sees its last N characters, marked `[...]`; 0 = all |
| `chunk_tokens` | 1024 | the thought is generated N tokens at a time with the loop check in between; 0 = one call, no loop check |
| `think_temperature` | `{"choice": 1.0, "noul": 1.0, "score": 1.0}` | the read-out after the thought is re-tempered from the type temperature to this one; a type left out is not re-tempered |
| `sampling` | `{"temperature": 0.6, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20}` | sampling of the thought |

Unknown keys and out-of-range values are refused when the server starts.

## GET /v1/models

`{"models": [{"name", "description", "release_date"}]}`. `release_date` comes from `decision_config.json`
(`release_date`), else the date of that file.

## GET /health

Status, model name and kind (`instant`, `auto_think` or `v1`), whether the server reads images, prompt attention, the
engine and its settings, the default controls, the largest think budget a request may ask for, and the context length
used for the room check. A server with
API keys returns only the status, model name and kind to a request without a valid key, so that the addresses and
settings of its engines stay private.

## Python

```python
import asyncio
from startlux_decide.backends.vllm import VLLMBackend
from startlux_decide.modelcfg import load_model_folder, load_tokenizer
from startlux_decide.pipeline import Decider

async def main():
    folder = load_model_folder("/models/StartLux-Decision-4B")
    engine = VLLMBackend(["http://127.0.0.1:8001"], load_tokenizer(folder.path))
    await engine.start()
    decider = Decider(folder, engine)
    result = await decider.decide(state, questions, decider.controls({"return_details": True}))
    print(result.answers, result.usage, result.timing_ms)
    await engine.close()

asyncio.run(main())
```

# Benchmarks

## Accuracy and calibration: `startlux-decide eval`

Input: JSONL, one request per line, with gold labels:

```json
{"id": "r1", "state": "...", "questions": {"team": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "...", "criteria": {...}}},
 "gold": {"team": "billing"}}
```

The label is an option id for a choice, `true` / `false` (or `"yes"` / `"no"`) for a yes/no question, and the level
index (0 = lowest) or a criteria key for a score. Questions without a label are sent but not scored.

```bash
startlux-decide eval --url http://127.0.0.1:8090 --data gold.jsonl --out run.jsonl --concurrency 16
startlux-decide eval --score run.jsonl                    # score a predictions file again
startlux-decide eval --compare run_a.jsonl run_b.jsonl    # paired comparison
startlux-decide eval ... --controls '{"think_mode": "never"}'   # merged into every request
```

Every request is sent with `return_details`. Per question, the predicted label is the choice, yes when P(yes) â‰¥ 0.5, or
the most probable level; its probability is the confidence.

| metric | definition |
|---|---|
| accuracy | share of scored questions whose predicted label is the gold label |
| ECE | top-label calibration error: 10 equal-width confidence bins, \|accuracy âˆ’ mean confidence\| per bin weighted by its share |
| Brier | sum over the options of (p âˆ’ 1[option is gold])Â², averaged (a yes/no question counts both options) |
| thought share | share of questions that thought (from the answers' details) |
| thought tokens | mean thought tokens over all questions, and over the questions that thought |

`--compare A B` pairs questions by request id and key (same gold label) and reports the agreement of the predicted
labels, both accuracies, the difference B âˆ’ A with a 95% bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples of requests, since the
questions of a request share their evidence), the both / only-A / only-B correct counts, the agreement of the gate's
decisions, and the largest change of any option's probability per question (mean and maximum). Use it to compare
engines, builds (BF16 against FP8, GGUF or MLX) and settings.

## Latency: `startlux-decide bench`

```bash
startlux-decide bench --url http://127.0.0.1:8090 --requests requests.jsonl --concurrency 1 --warmup 20 \
    --out latency_summary.csv --rows latency_rows.csv
```

The requests file has one `/v1/systemone` body per line (`id` and `gold` fields are ignored). Every request is sent
with `return_details`. Per request:

| column | measured by | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `client_ms` | the client | from sending the request to receiving the whole answer |
| `wall_ms` | the server | the request inside the server, from validation to the answers |
| `first_pass_sum_ms` | the server | sum over the questions of their first-pass engine calls |
| `thought_span_ms` | the server | from the first thought chunk sent to the last one received, over all questions (0 without a thought) |
| `after_thought_sum_ms` | the server | sum over the questions of the read-outs after a thought |
| `questions`, `thought_questions`, `thought_tokens` | the server | per request |

The server's timings wrap the engine calls themselves: prompt rendering and tokenization are outside the per-phase
times and inside `wall_ms`. Thought spans include the wait for a wave (up to `--wave-gather`, 0.3 s, per chunk) on
vLLM. The summary CSV has n, mean, median, p80 and p95 of every column over the requests that succeeded (percentiles
by linear interpolation between order statistics).

Latency depends on the engine, the GPU, the share of questions that think and the load. For numbers comparable with the
published ones measure one request at a time (`--concurrency 1`) after a warm-up, on servers with the release flags and
nothing else running on their GPUs, and report the share of requests with a thought next to the latency.

## Reproducing the published numbers

Serve the folder on vLLM with the defaults (`startlux-decide serve --model DIR --launch-vllm --gpus ...`) and send the
benchmark's requests. The defaults are the settings of the release runs (README, "Published numbers"); for AutoThink
the mixture 0.75 is the one the published numbers use (it was applied to the stored first and second read-outs of every
question). Thoughts are sampled, so a rerun of an AutoThink benchmark differs from the published run within sampling
noise; Instant read-outs are deterministic up to the numerics of batching.

# Deployment

What the server and the engines do with images, long prompts and the two model releases, and which engine settings to switch on or off. Every setting below was measured; [engines.md](engines.md) and [quantization.md](quantization.md) have the reasons and the numbers.

## Deployment settings

`launch-vllm` reads the vLLM version and picks the flags below; on vLLM 0.31 the settings are those of the reference
deployment (prefix caching and chunked prefill on, 8,192 batched tokens per step).

| engine | setting | on or off | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM 0.19.1 | `--no-enable-prefix-caching` | prefix caching off | on 0.19.1 it moves 2.6% of the read-outs of these hybrid models by more than 0.05, without an error |
| vLLM 0.19.1 | `--no-enable-chunked-prefill`, `--max-num-batched-tokens` equal to `--max-model-len` | chunked prefill off | on 0.19.1 a prompt split across scheduler steps is misread |
| vLLM 0.31 | `--enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 8192` | on for AutoThink and v1 | on 0.31 prefix caching works on these models only with chunked prefill, and with both on the 27B AutoThink model gave the same answer as on 0.19.1 for 99.88% of 823 questions; a thought no longer re-reads its prompt |
| vLLM 0.31 | `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` | on when the folder holds MTP weights; `--no-mtp` turns it off | the MTP layer proposes 3 tokens per step, so thoughts are generated faster; the thoughts kept their length distribution in our check at 4B, 9B and 27B |
| vLLM 0.31 | thought as one streamed request (`--thought-generation`, default `auto`) | on | no chunk re-sends the prompt and the thought so far; the loop detector still looks at the thought every 1,024 tokens and ends a looping one there |
| vLLM, Instant | prefix caching and chunked prefill off, no MTP, on every version | required | the Instant plugin needs every prompt prefilled whole in one step |
| vLLM | `--logprobs-mode processed_logprobs --max-logprobs 26` | on | the read-out returns exactly the option letters |
| vLLM | `--generation-config vllm` | on | keeps the folder's top-k and top-p away from the read-out |
| vLLM | prompt-bidirectional plugin (`launch-vllm` sets `STARTLUX_PREFIX_BIDIR=1`), vLLM 0.19.1 or 0.31.0 | on for Instant | Instant models were trained to read the prompt bidirectionally; without it they answer as a different model |
| vLLM | thought waves (`--waves` / `--no-waves`; default: on for servers older than 0.31) | on with vLLM 0.19.1 | on 0.19.1 a thought that joins a running decode batch can turn into a loop; 0.31 fixed this |
| vLLM | `--quantization fp8` | optional, 27B only | within 0.2 points at 27B; costs the 4B Instant model 1.3 DecideBench points and shifts the decision to think |
| vLLM | `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` | off | refused by the plugin, and it shifts the decision to think |
| vLLM 0.31 | `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":8,"video":0}' --mm-processor-kwargs ... --trust-request-chat-template` | on for folders with a vision tower; `--no-images` turns it off | image calls carry the client's pass-through chat template, and the server resizes images within the package's bounds; Instant servers also get `--skip-mm-profiling` (with vLLM's profile of 256 full-size images the 4B Instant server did not start) |
| vLLM | `--max-model-len` | on 0.31 the folder's native 262,144, Instant 131,072; on 0.19.1 65,536 | an Instant prompt is read in one step, and on 0.31 that step crashed vLLM at 196,000 (27B) and 256,000 tokens (4B); prompts beyond the limit get a 422 |
| llama.cpp | GGUF converted with [`patches/llama.cpp/0002`](../patches/llama.cpp) (or `--override-kv qwen35.attention.causal=bool:false`) | on for Instant | marks the prompt as bidirectional; read causally, the 4B Instant model loses 27 DecideBench points |
| llama.cpp | stock llama-server: `--parallel 1 --ctx-checkpoints 0 -b 16384 -ub 16384`; or [`patches/llama.cpp/0001`](../patches/llama.cpp) with any `--parallel` | required for Instant | otherwise prompts are batched or split, which costs the 4B Instant model 7.7 DecideBench points |
| llama.cpp | prompt cache (`cache_prompt`) | off (the backend sends false) | a reused prefix would break the bidirectional reading |
| llama.cpp | GPU sampling (`-bs`) | off | it changed read-outs by up to 0.40 in log-probability |
| llama.cpp | quantization | Q8_0 recommended | Q4_K_M costs 1.6 to 3.8 DecideBench points at 2B to 9B |

## Images and long inputs

A request can carry images as part of its evidence, and a prompt can run to 262,144 tokens (256K), the models' native
context. This is v1's request format.

```bash
curl -s localhost:8090/v1/systemone -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "state": "Photo taken at delivery: <image>",
  "questions": {"damaged": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is the parcel damaged?"}},
  "images": ["data:image/jpeg;base64,'"$(base64 < parcel.jpg | tr -d '\n')"'"]
}'
```

- `images` is a list of base64 strings or data URIs. `<image>` in the state marks where each image goes, one mark per
  image, in order. Without marks the images come first (as `Image 1:`, `Image 2:` ... when there are several),
  followed by the state.
- Each image is resized to at most 1,048,576 pixels, keeping its aspect ratio (`--max-pixels`), and becomes one token
  per 32 Ã— 32 pixels: a 1024 Ã— 1024 photo is 1,024 tokens. Every question of the request reads the same images. At
  most 8 images per request (`--max-images`); `--no-images` serves text only.
- Images work on vLLM 0.31 or later, on the transformers engine, on llama.cpp (llama-server started with the model's
  `mmproj-*-F16.gguf` file; without it a request with images gets a 422) and on MLX (mlx-vlm folders), for v1 and
  v1.1 folders (all of them keep the vision tower).
- Checked on vLLM 0.31 against the transformers engine with the same 12 image questions: the same top option in 59 of
  60 read-outs over 4B and 27B AutoThink, 4B and 27B Instant and v1 4B, largest probability difference 0.04 to 0.09
  per model. The same questions without their images differ by at most 0.012, and both engines' image processors give
  identical pixels: the image differences come from the two engines' vision paths (also in the causal folders, which
  do not use the Instant plugin). Read-outs with images are therefore close to, not equal to, the reference.

Long inputs:

- On vLLM 0.31 the servers accept prompts up to the folder's native 262,144 tokens, and Instant servers up to 131,072
  (`launch-vllm` defaults; on 0.19.1 65,536 as before). `--max-model-len` sets the serving limit (65,536 is a
  good choice on 80 GB GPUs); a longer prompt gets a 422 with the engine's reason.
- AutoThink and v1 folders read a long state once per request: the package reads the beginning that the questions
  share into vLLM's prefix cache, sends every question of the request to that server, and each question then reads
  only its own part. A thought re-reads nothing either.
- Instant folders read every prompt whole, in one step, because their prompt attention is bidirectional: a request
  with n questions reads its state n times, and one step must hold a whole prompt. On vLLM 0.31 that step crashed the
  server for a 256,000-token prompt (4B) and a 196,000-token prompt (27B), which is why Instant servers stop at
  131,072 tokens.
- What a long prompt costs, one H200 per server, the answer in the first lines of the state, nothing cached before:

  | model | 32,000 tokens | 128,000 | 256,000 | the same state again |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 4B AutoThink | 0.65 s | 3.8 s | 11.0 s | 0.14 / 0.45 / 0.96 s |
  | 27B AutoThink | | 15.9 s | 42.0 s | 0.46 / 1.04 s |
  | 4B Instant | 0.78 s | 7.3 s | | every question reads it again |
  | 27B Instant | | 24.7 s | | every question reads it again |

  Every answer was right. A second question over the same state added 0.2 to 1.3 s to the causal models and nearly
  doubled the time of the 4B Instant model (1.5 s at 32,000 tokens, 12.7 s at 128,000). At the full context the 4B AutoThink server's cache holds 13.7 prompts of 262,144
  tokens, the 27B's 4.2 ([engines.md](engines.md) has the details).

## Compatibility

The engine serves the decisions of both releases, with images and long inputs:

| release | folders | how it answers |
|---|---|---|
| v1.1 | Instant and AutoThink folders (0.8B to 27B) | as above |
| v1 | `decision_config.json` with `"format": "StartLux-Decision-v1"` (0.8B, 2B, 4B, 9B, 27B and 35B-A3B) | one pass by default, with the same prompts as v1.1. A request may still set `think_mode` to `auto` or `always`, but v1 was not trained to think |

Images work for both releases on vLLM 0.31, transformers, llama.cpp (with an mmproj file) and MLX (mlx-vlm folders),
and the 256K context on vLLM 0.31 and transformers. The v1 4B folder, served by this engine, read 12 image questions
with the same top option as the transformers engine and answered a 128,000-token request correctly in 4.1 s.

## Published numbers

The published numbers were measured on vLLM 0.19.1 with the defaults there: the vLLM flags of `launch-vllm`, the
read-out temperatures of each folder, and for AutoThink the gate 0.9, budget 4,096, thought chunks of 1,024 tokens with
the loop detector between them, the last 4,000 characters of the thought read after it, think temperature 1.0 and the
mixture 0.75. On vLLM 0.31 the defaults change how the thought is produced, not the decision rule: the thought is one
streamed request, prefix caching is on and MTP proposes 3 tokens per step (see Deployment settings). The engine's default
gate is now 0.6, so serve with `--gate 0.9` on vLLM and use `startlux-decide eval` on the benchmark's requests;
[benchmarks.md](benchmarks.md) describes the measurement of accuracy and latency, and
[engines.md](engines.md) lists where this package differs from the code of those runs (answers' confidence
field, usage counts and edge cases; never the probabilities).

# Engines

Every engine implements two primitives (`startlux_decide/backends/base.py`):

* `readout(prompt, letter_ids)`: one forward pass, the log-probabilities of the option letters as the next token;
* `generate(prompt, max_tokens, sampling, stop, seed)`: a sampled continuation, for the thoughts of AutoThink models.

Engines that stream a thought safely (vLLM 0.31 or later) also implement `generate_stream`, the same continuation as
one streamed request; closing the stream early ends the request in the engine.

Prompt rendering, temperatures, the gate, the thought loop, the mixture, knock-out lists and the answer format are
the package's own code and the same for every engine.

## vLLM (default)

vLLM 0.19.1 (the version of the release runs) or 0.31.0, one OpenAI-compatible server per GPU. Both versions are
validated with the Instant plugin ([vllm_bidirectional.md](vllm_bidirectional.md#vllm-versions)).
`startlux-decide launch-vllm` (or `serve --launch-vllm`) reads the vLLM version of the Python that runs vLLM and starts
the servers with these flags:

```
all:      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs --max-logprobs 26
          --generation-config vllm --served-model-name m
          --max-model-len: 0.31 or later 262144 (the folder's max_position_embeddings), Instant folders 131072;
                           0.19.1 65536; --max-model-len N sets it
0.19.1, and Instant folders on every version:
          --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens <max-model-len>
AutoThink and v1 folders on 0.31 or later:
          --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
          --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'   (folders with MTP weights; --no-mtp: off)
images, on 0.31 or later for folders with a vision tower (--no-images: text only):
          --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":8,"video":0}' --trust-request-chat-template
          --mm-processor-kwargs '{"size":{"longest_edge":1048576,"shortest_edge":65536}}'
          (Instant folders also --skip-mm-profiling)
text only (0.19.1, --no-images, folders without a vision tower):
          --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}'
```

| flag | why |
|---|---|
| `--logprobs-mode processed_logprobs`, `--max-logprobs 26` | a read-out asks for the log-probabilities of up to 26 letters with `allowed_token_ids`; processed log-probabilities are taken after that mask, so exactly the letters come back. With raw log-probabilities the top 26 of the whole vocabulary come back and letters go missing |
| `--generation-config vllm` | otherwise vLLM applies the folder's generation_config (top_k, top_p) to every request, the read-out included, and letters outside the top k get no probability |
| `--no-enable-prefix-caching` (0.19.1, Instant) | on vLLM 0.19.1 prefix caching changes answers of these hybrid models (Gated DeltaNet layers) silently: in our tests it moved 2.6% of ordinary and 16% of knocked-out read-outs by more than 0.05 |
| `--no-enable-chunked-prefill` (0.19.1, Instant) | on 0.19.1 chunked prefill also changed read-outs of long prompts silently, and the Instant plugin needs every prompt prefilled whole |
| `--max-num-batched-tokens` = `--max-model-len` (0.19.1, Instant) | a whole prompt fits in one step |
| `--enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill` (AutoThink and v1 on 0.31) | on vLLM 0.31 prefix caching works on these hybrid models only together with chunked prefill. With both on, the 27B AutoThink model gave the same answer as on 0.19.1 for 99.88% of 823 questions (0.12% of read-outs moved by more than 0.05), and a thought request no longer re-reads the prompt it shares with the first read-out |
| `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` (AutoThink and v1 on 0.31) | the prefill chunk; the setting of the reference deployment |
| `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` (0.31, folders with MTP weights) | multi-token prediction: the MTP layer proposes 3 tokens per step and the model checks them, so a thought is generated faster with the same sampling distribution. A folder has MTP weights when its config declares `mtp_num_hidden_layers` and it holds `mtp.*` tensors; on 4B, 9B and 27B with 3 draft tokens the thoughts kept their length distribution in our check. `--no-mtp` turns it off. The Instant plugin refuses speculative decoding |
| `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}'` (text only) | no memory for the vision tower's inputs |
| `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":8,"video":0}'`, `--mm-processor-kwargs`, `--trust-request-chat-template` (images) | at most 8 images per prompt (`--max-images`), resized within the bounds of the package (`--max-pixels`); an image call carries the client's pass-through chat template (below) |
| `--max-model-len` | on 0.31 the native context of the folders, 262,144 tokens, and 131,072 for Instant folders (their one-step prefill of a 196,000 to 256,000-token prompt crashed vLLM 0.31, see [vllm_bidirectional.md](vllm_bidirectional.md#known-limits)); a lower serving limit (for example `--max-model-len 65536` on 80 GB GPUs) costs nothing for shorter prompts |

At start the vLLM client reads the served model name and context length from `/v1/models` and sends a probe read-out
over all 26 letters; a server without the read-out flags is refused with the flags to add. It cannot see the caching
flags: servers started by hand must use the flags above.

**Thoughts on vLLM.** At start the client reads every server's version from `/version`. On vLLM 0.31 or later a
thought is one streamed request (`thought_generation` `stream`, the default there). The loop detector looks at the
thought each time another 1,024 tokens have arrived and once more when the budget ends it, the points where the
chunked path runs it; a looping thought is cut as in the chunked path (the reasoning and the start of the loop are
kept) and its request is closed, which ends it in vLLM. With MTP an event of the stream can carry up to 4 tokens, so a
check can run up to 3 tokens past 1,024, 2,048 or 3,072. On older vLLM (or with `thought_generation` `chunked`) a
thought is generated 1,024 tokens at a time; each chunk re-sends the prompt and the thought so far with its own seed,
and the loop detector runs between chunks. Both use the prompt with the forced start, the seed of the first chunk (from
a hash of the thinking prompt; later chunks add 7,919 each), temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, the stop string
`</think>`, the budget and the CUT line. All calls of one question go to the same server; questions are spread round
robin over the servers.

**Waves (vLLM 0.19.1).** On vLLM 0.19.1 the state of hybrid models gets corrupted when new generation requests join a
decode batch that is already running: in our tests 25 to 35% of thoughts turned into garbage loops. The client
therefore sends the chunked thought requests of each server in waves: everything queued goes out together, and the
next wave starts only when the whole wave has finished. With waves no thought was corrupted (0 of 183). A request waits
up to 0.3 s for its wave to fill (`--wave-gather`) and at most 128 requests go in a wave (`--wave-max`). Read-outs are
prefill only and are sent at any time. vLLM 0.31 fixed the corruption (0 of 183 thoughts unclosed at 64 requests in
flight, without waves), so waves are on only for servers older than 0.31 or that do not report a version;
`--waves` and `--no-waves` decide instead. A request that asks for `stream` on such a server gets a 422.

**Images on vLLM** (0.31 or later). A call whose prompt holds images goes to `/v1/chat/completions` instead of
`/v1/completions`: one user message whose parts are the pieces of the package's rendered prompt with the images (data
URIs) between them, and a chat template that writes the parts back to back and the image placeholder
(`<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>`) for each image. vLLM therefore reads exactly the package's prompt; its
image processor resizes each image within the server's bounds (`--mm-processor-kwargs`, which the launcher sets to the
package's 65,536 to 1,048,576 pixels; the package counts the tokens with the same rule), puts each image's tokens at its
placeholder and gives them their multimodal positions. The servers need `--trust-request-chat-template` (the template
comes with each call). Read-outs, thoughts (chunked or streamed) and prefix-cache fills all take this path when the
request has images. On Instant servers the plugin reads the image tokens bidirectionally like every other prompt token.

**Long prompts.** The servers take prompts up to `--max-model-len` (on vLLM 0.31: 262,144 tokens for causal folders,
131,072 for Instant folders). A longer prompt is refused by vLLM, and the request gets a 422 with vLLM's reason. Causal folders (AutoThink, v1) read
long prompts in steps of 8,192 tokens (chunked prefill) into the prefix cache; when the questions of a request share a
beginning of 4,096 tokens or more (their state), the package reads that beginning once (a one-token request) and then
sends every question of the request to the same server, so each question reads only its own part, and a thought reads
neither the prompt nor the thought so far again. Instant folders must read each prompt whole in one step: their servers
run with `--max-num-batched-tokens` equal to the context and no prefix cache, so a request with n questions over a long
state reads the state n times, and one step must fit a whole prompt.

Measured on vLLM 0.31, one H200 per server (five servers side by side on one node), a decision whose answer is in the
first lines of a long state, the state not yet in any cache:

| model | 32,000 tokens | 128,000 | 256,000 | two questions over the same state | the same request again |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4B AutoThink | 0.65 s | 3.8 s | 11.0 s | 0.81 / 4.4 / 12.1 s | 0.14 / 0.45 / 0.96 s |
| 27B AutoThink | | 15.9 s | 42.0 s | 16.4 / 43.3 s | 0.46 / 1.04 s |
| v1 4B | | 4.1 s | | 4.7 s | 0.46 s |
| 4B Instant | 0.78 s | 7.3 s | crashed (see above) | 1.5 / 12.7 s | (no cache) |
| 27B Instant | | 24.7 s | not at 196,000 | | (no cache) |

Every answer was right (the choice with probability 0.997 or more). The second question of a causal request costs
the reading of its own part; at 256,000 tokens the package's own work (rendering and counting the prompts of each
question) is most of the 0.96 s of a request whose state is cached. KV cache at the native context (0.88 of the GPU):
4B AutoThink 3.60 million tokens (13.7 prompts of 262,144), 27B AutoThink 1.09 million (4.2 prompts), v1 4B 3.11
million; an Instant server reserves the activations of a whole-prompt step on top (4B at 262,144: 2.96 million
tokens of cache; 27B at 131,072: 0.79 million).

**One process.** The decision server is one Python process; prompt rendering and token counting run in its event loop
and cost about 0.4 ms per question with a short state and about 10 ms per question of 8,000 prompt tokens (measured
with the models' tokenizer on one CPU core). For high request rates over many GPUs, run several `serve` processes, each
with its share of the vLLM servers, behind a load balancer, as the release runs did (one per GPU).

**Instant folders on vLLM** need the plugin in this package, which makes vLLM read the prompt bidirectionally in the
full-attention layers. It is a vLLM general plugin (entry point `startlux_prefix_bidir`), active when the folder is
prompt-bidirectional and `STARTLUX_PREFIX_BIDIR=1` is set. The launcher sets the variable, checks that vLLM's Python
sees the plugin, and refuses to continue unless every server log shows "prefix-bidirectional prompt attention ON".
Without the plugin vLLM reads such a folder causally, without notice, and answers as a different model. vLLM 0.31
runs a new model runner by default (V2); the plugin patches it as well as the V1 runner, and a vLLM worker whose runner
it did not patch refuses an Instant folder at start. Details and test results:
[vllm_bidirectional.md](vllm_bidirectional.md).

## transformers

In-process reference on PyTorch (`--backend transformers`, extra `[transformers]`, transformers 5.8). One prompt per
forward pass, one call at a time: for checks, not for serving load. Images go through the folder's processor with the
same resize bounds and the model's vision tower; an Instant folder reads the result (image features in place,
multimodal positions) with its bidirectional prompt attention. Instant folders are read with the bidirectional
prompt attention they were trained with (`backends/bidirectional.py`, checked on the model at start: the causal path
equals the stock forward, padding never reaches a token, a late token reaches the first position). Thoughts use
transformers' sampler, so they are not token-identical to vLLM's for the same seed. On CUDA install
flash-linear-attention and causal-conv1d; without them transformers runs the linear-attention layers on a plain
PyTorch path that is more than ten times slower. On a machine without a GPU those two packages must not be installed
(they would be called on CPU tensors).

## llama.cpp

`--backend llamacpp --llamacpp-url URL` puts the package in front of llama-server for GGUF builds; the model folder
still provides the tokenizer and `decision_config.json`. A read-out sends the token ids with `n_predict` 1,
`post_sampling_probs`, a logit bias of +100 on the k option letters and `top_k` = k, so the sampler keeps exactly the
letters and their probabilities are the softmax over the letters alone (the same bias on every letter does not change
their relative probabilities); every other sampler is neutral. Thoughts use the sampling settings of vLLM and its
sampler order (temperature first, then top-k and top-p; llama.cpp's default applies top-p first). Prompt caching is
off. Tested with llama.cpp b11549.

**Images on llama.cpp.** Start llama-server with the model's mmproj file (`--mmproj mmproj-...-F16.gguf`, the F16 file in
the same repository as the GGUF) and `--image-min-tokens 64 --image-max-tokens 1024` (the package's pixel bounds in
tokens). `/props` then reports the vision modality and the server's media marker, and the backend takes images
(`engine.images` in `/health` is true). A call with images sends `"prompt": {"prompt_string": ..., "multimodal_data":
[...]}`: the rendered prompt as text with the media marker at each image's place, and the images as base64 PNGs. llama.cpp
tokenizes the text itself, because an object prompt cannot carry token ids (its count equalled the Hugging Face
tokenizer's on every image request of the smoke test), and adds `<|vision_start|>` and `<|vision_end|>` around each
image. The backend has already resized every image with PIL (bicubic) to the processor size, so the server's own resize
does nothing and the pixels are the ones vLLM reads. After every image call it compares the server's `tokens_evaluated`
with its own count (text tokens, plus 2 and the image's tokens for each image; `/tokenize` tells a difference in the text
from one in the images) and raises when they differ, for example when the server was started with a smaller
`--image-max-tokens` and resized an image. Without `--mmproj`, a request with images gets a 422. Text-only calls are what
they were.

**Instant folders** need non-causal attention over the prompt in the full-attention layers. A released Instant GGUF
carries `qwen35.attention.causal = false` (written by `patches/llama.cpp/0002-...`), and the prompt must be evaluated
alone and in one micro-batch. `STARTLUX_LLAMACPP_BIDIR` says how the server provides this:

| value | server | what the backend does |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` (default) | any | reads `/props` once at start: a server that reports patch 0003 (`mtmd_prompt_whole_when_non_causal`) works as `server`, any other as `request` |
| `request` | llama-server with `patches/llama.cpp/0001-...`, any `--parallel` | sends `prompt_bidirectional` with every read-out and checks the echo; a stock server is an error |
| `server` | stock llama-server with `--parallel 1 --ctx-checkpoints 0 -b 16384 -ub 16384` | relies on the non-causal context of the file |
| `off` | any | reads the prompt causally: a different model, for measuring that cost only |

A stock llama-server reports nothing about its context, so `auto` takes it for a `request` server and the first read-out
of an Instant folder fails with a message that names `server`: set `STARTLUX_LLAMACPP_BIDIR=server` for it. The mode in
use is `engine.bidir_mode` in `/health`.

**Instant folders with images.** The text and the image embeddings of a prompt must be read in one micro-batch with
non-causal attention. Use mode `server` (`auto` picks it for a server with patch 0003; for any other, set
`STARTLUX_LLAMACPP_BIDIR=server`) with a non-causal GGUF and `--parallel 1 --ctx-checkpoints 0 -b N -ub N`, N at least the
longest prompt including its image tokens. The per-request mode (`request`, patch 0001) does not cover images and is
refused with a 422. Stock b11549 splits such a prompt into three micro-batches (text, image, text): on 32 image
questions the 4B Instant Q8_0 read-outs then differ from BF16 by 0.022 on average (largest 0.22), and with
`patches/llama.cpp/0003-server-mtmd-prompt-whole-on-non-causal-context.patch` by 0.0055 (largest 0.06). The patched
server says so in `/props` (`mtmd_prompt_whole_when_non_causal`); the backend warns, and reports
`image_prompt: split (stock server)` in `/health`, when an Instant folder with images is served without it.

Measured on one H200 against vLLM BF16 (823 questions): BF16 GGUF top-1 agreement 99.5 to 100% (two vLLM runs: 99.9%),
Q8_0 99.4 to 99.6%, Q4_K_M 97.0 to 99.2%. On DecideBench the 4B Instant model loses 0.6 points as Q8_0, 3.1 as Q4_K_M,
7.7 on a stock server with default settings and 26 when its prompt is read causally ([benchmarks.md](benchmarks.md)).
llama.cpp answers short Instant requests faster than vLLM and long ones up to three times more slowly, because it
evaluates the bidirectional prompts of a request one at a time.

## MLX

`--backend mlx` (extra `[mlx]`, Apple Silicon) runs the folder's own decoder in mlx-vlm and builds the input itself.
It reads mlx-vlm folders (`mlx_vlm.convert`: the text model 8-bit or 4-bit, the vision tower kept in BF16), the BF16
release folders, and text-only MLX folders (images then get a 422). Instant folders are read with the bidirectional
prompt attention they were trained with (the full-attention layers see every token of the one-pass input, the
linear-attention layers stay causal; a self-check at load time confirms it). AutoThink thoughts are sampled with the
request's settings and seed. Images follow the vLLM flow: the folder's image processor, the vision tower's features at
the image tokens, the processor's three-axis positions. One call runs at a time.

## Parity with the release runs

The golden test (`tests/test_golden.py`) runs this package's pipeline and the per-question pipeline of the runs behind
the published AutoThink numbers side by side on a fake vLLM, over random requests and settings: the requests sent to
vLLM (every read-out prompt, thought chunk, seed and sampling setting) and the probabilities, choices, scores and thought
token counts are identical, bit for bit. Instant read-outs are the one-pass read-out of those runs (the same path with
thinking off). Deliberate differences, none of which changes a probability of an answered question:

| | release runs | this package |
|---|---|---|
| `confidence` of choice and score answers | the top probability | TypeSafe's definitions (above) |
| score `legend` when criteria is `{key: level}` | levels in the order given | levels in the order they are shown to the model (numeric keys ascending) |
| choice with one option | refused (422) | answered with probability 1 |
| `mix` 0 | meant "the read-out after the thought only" | means "the first read-out only" (the formula) |
| `usage.input_tokens` of knocked-out lists | the final round's prompt | every round's prompts |
| request controls | `think_mode` only, unknown values ignored | `think_mode`, `gate`, `think_budget`, `mix`, `thought_generation`, details; bad values give 422 |
| thoughts on vLLM 0.31 | (not run) | one streamed request (the chunked path on request); the golden test runs the chunked path, and `tests/test_stream.py` shows that with one token per stream event the streamed path gives the same thoughts and probabilities as the chunked one on the fake vLLM |
| malformed body, empty `questions` | 400 | 422, FastAPI-style `detail` |
| `cache_mode`, `--rep-pen`, `--stop-loops`, `--loop-version` 1 and 2 | test switches | not carried over (the release used none of them) |
| backend errors | 422 for a refusal, otherwise an unstructured 500 | 422 for a refusal, 502 after four tries |

# none_probability

Every `choice` answer of `startlux-decide serve` carries `none_probability`: how strongly the model believes that
none of the listed options is right. This page explains where the number comes from, how to read it, why we suggest
0.2 as the threshold, and where it is not reliable.

## Where it comes from

The model answers a choice question by reading the probability of each option's letter at one position of the
prompt; it does not generate text. With `none_check` (on by default in `serve`) the engine adds one more option at the
end of the list, "None of the above", with its own letter, and the model scores it like any other option.
`none_probability` is the share of the read-out that goes to that extra letter. The listed options' probabilities are
then scaled up to sum to 1, so `probabilities` keeps its usual meaning, and `choice` is the most likely listed option.
With `"allow_none": true`, `choice` is null when "None of the above" is the most likely option.

For an AutoThink answer that went through a thought, the final probabilities mix the read-out before the thought and
the one after it (0.25 and 0.75 by default), and `none_probability` is the mixed value. The extra option also takes
part in the confidence gate: a question whose read-out gives a lot to "None of the above" has no listed option above
the gate and therefore gets a thought.

An example. Asked what 1 + 1 is, with only 5 and 10 as options, the model gives about 0.02 to 5, 0.01 to 10 and 0.97 to
"None of the above". The answer is `none_probability` 0.97, `probabilities` {5: 0.67, 10: 0.33} and `choice` 5 (null
with `allow_none`).

The models were not trained on questions with this extra option. `none_probability` is how they read the words "None
of the above" on their own, which is why it works well as a signal but is not a calibrated probability.

## How we measured it

We took every choice question with 3 to 24 options and a known right answer from DecisionPivot (6,007 questions) and
the public part of Decision Index 0.3 (45,499 questions), leaving out questions whose options already offered "none",
"other" or similar. Each question was asked twice with the extra option: as published, and with its right answer
removed, so that no listed option was right. The model was StartLux-Decision-v1.1-27B-AutoThink on vLLM, with thinking
on (`think_mode` `auto`) unless a row says otherwise. All numbers below come from that run of 51,506 questions; the
smaller models were not measured.

Adding the extra option does not cost accuracy: on the published questions the most likely listed option was right
84.66% of the time with the extra option and 84.66% without it (78.53% and 78.50% in one pass).

## How to read it

Read `none_probability` as an alarm score, not as an exact probability. The model is reluctant to pick "None of the
above", so its numbers run low. In a set made half of published questions and half of questions without a right
answer, this is the share of questions that really had no right answer, by `none_probability`:

| `none_probability` | 0.05 to 0.1 | 0.1 to 0.2 | 0.2 to 0.3 | 0.3 to 0.5 | 0.5 and above |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no right answer | 56% | 77% | 87% | 93% | 96% to 99% |

As a ranking it is strong: given one question without a right answer and one with, the first has the higher
`none_probability` 92% of the time (AUROC 0.920; 0.892 in one pass).

## Why 0.2

| Threshold | Questions without a right answer caught | Published questions flagged by mistake |
|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | 73.7% | 4.5% |
| **0.2** | **66.3%** | **2.2%** |
| 0.3 | 61.5% | 1.6% |
| 0.5 | 53.5% | 1.0% |

We suggest treating `none_probability` â‰¥ 0.2 as "no listed option fits" for four reasons.

1. **False alarms stay near 2%.** At 0.2 about one well-posed question in 45 is flagged. Going down to 0.1 catches
   7 points more but doubles the false alarms to 4.5%. Going up to 0.5 halves them to 1.0% but misses 13 points more.
2. **Above 0.2 a flag is usually right.** Questions between 0.2 and 0.3 had no right answer 87% of the time in the
   half-and-half set; between 0.1 and 0.2 it was 77%, and between 0.05 and 0.1 close to a coin toss (56%).
3. **It holds across settings.** The lowest threshold that keeps false alarms under 3% is 0.15 with thinking and 0.19 in
   one pass; 0.2 keeps both under 3% (2.2% and 2.6%), and false alarms are 2.5% on DecisionPivot and 2.2% on Decision
   Index.
4. **Lower cuts flag too many good questions.** The best single cut by Youden's J is lower (0.06), but around it about
   one published question in ten is flagged (10.4% at 0.05), which is too many for most applications.

What a flag means also depends on how often your traffic has no right answer. Share of flagged questions that really
had no right answer:

| Questions without a right answer in your traffic | 1% | 5% | 20% |
|---|---|---|---|
| threshold 0.1 | 14% | 46% | 80% |
| threshold 0.2 | 23% | 61% | 88% |
| threshold 0.5 | 35% | 74% | 93% |

Use 0.1 when a missed problem is expensive and a person reviews every flag, 0.5 when a flag interrupts a user, and 0.2
otherwise. If you can, set the threshold on a few hundred of your own questions.

## Where it is not reliable

It works best when a question has one answer that can be checked against the state: rule and policy decisions,
extraction, fact checks, entailment, arithmetic. There 77% of the questions without a right answer are caught at 0.2,
with 1.5% false alarms.

It is weak in two situations, and a threshold cannot fix either:

- **When "none of them" is not well defined.** For preferences between acceptable options (which plan, which
  consensus statement people would choose) and for the choice of a move in a game, removing the best option still
  leaves a best option, and the model does not call the rest wrong. Detection was 0% to 13% on these tasks. Comparisons
  with a clear right answer are not affected: picking the better of two responses to a prompt was caught 83% of the
  time.
- **When the model does not know the answer.** On very hard questions (graduate-level science, expert exams) the model
  cannot tell that the right answer is missing: 16% to 47% were caught.

False alarms are higher than average where options are unusual or long: matching captions to cartoons (25%), choosing
an element on a web page (14%) and long multi-step reasoning stories (12%).

In these settings add your own "none of these" option to the list, or check the answer another way.

## Thinking

Questions without a right answer make AutoThink think more often: 78% of them got a thought against 51% of published
questions, and their thoughts were longer (544 against 290 thought tokens per question on average). Thinking also helps
the detection: 66.3% caught at 0.2 against 57.4% in one pass.

## Using it

```python
answer = response["answers"]["route"]
if answer["none_probability"] >= 0.2:
    escalate_to_a_person(answer)          # or ask again with more options
else:
    act_on(answer["choice"], answer["confidence"])
```

`none_check` adds one letter to every choice read-out and nothing else. Send `"none_check": false` in a request, or start
the server with `--no-none-check`, to leave the extra option out; answers then carry no `none_probability`. Send
`"allow_none": true` to get `choice: null` when "None of the above" wins. A server started with `--allow-none` does
that by default, and a request or a question can still send `"allow_none": false`.

# Quantization

`startlux-decide quantize fp8|gguf|mlx` prints the steps below (or runs them with `--run`). It checks that the tools
are there and downloads nothing.

## FP8 in vLLM

No separate build: vLLM quantizes the weights to FP8 when it loads the folder.

```bash
startlux-decide launch-vllm --model /models/StartLux-Decision-4B --gpus 0 --quantization fp8
```

This adds `--quantization fp8` to every server. The KV cache stays BF16 (the Instant plugin refuses an FP8 KV cache).

## GGUF for llama.cpp

AutoThink folders, and Instant folders when the llama.cpp tree has the converter patch `patches/llama.cpp/0002-convert-qwen35-prompt-bidirectional.patch` (it marks the GGUF non-causal; the command checks for it). For images, convert the vision encoder once with `convert_hf_to_gguf.py MODEL --mmproj --outtype f16` and pass the file to llama-server with `--mmproj`. With a llama.cpp checkout that has a build of `llama-quantize`:

```bash
startlux-decide quantize gguf --model /models/StartLux-Decision-4B --out /models/4B-gguf --llama-cpp ~/llama.cpp --type Q8_0 --run
llama-server -m /models/4B-gguf/model-Q8_0.gguf -ngl 99 -c 65536 --port 8081
startlux-decide serve --model /models/4B-gguf --backend llamacpp --llamacpp-url http://127.0.0.1:8081
```

The first step runs `convert_hf_to_gguf.py --outtype bf16` with the current Python (which needs llama.cpp's conversion
requirements), then `llama-quantize` (unless `--type BF16`), and copies the tokenizer files, `config.json` and
`decision_config.json` next to the GGUF file: the package renders the prompts and reads the letters itself. llama.cpp
must be recent enough to know the model's architecture. With `--parallel N`, llama-server splits `-c` over N slots; the
package takes the per-slot context from `/props` for the room check of thoughts.

`quantize gguf` makes the text decoder only. Images need the model's vision encoder in a separate mmproj file, which the
released GGUF repositories carry as an F16 file (`mmproj-*-F16.gguf`); see [engines.md](engines.md#llamacpp).

## MLX

Instant and AutoThink folders, on Apple Silicon. The text model is quantized (affine, group size 64), the vision tower
stays BF16, so the folder still reads images:

```bash
startlux-decide quantize mlx --model /models/StartLux-Decision-4B --out /models/4B-mlx-8bit --bits 8 --run
startlux-decide serve --model /models/4B-mlx-8bit --backend mlx
```

## Instant folders

A GGUF build of an Instant (prompt-bidirectional) folder must be read with the bidirectional prompt it was trained
with: convert it with `patches/llama.cpp/0002-...` (the released files already carry the flag) and serve it as
described in [engines.md](engines.md#llamacpp). Read causally, the build answers as a different model. The MLX engine reads
Instant folders bidirectionally, so MLX builds of them are fine.

## Measure every build again

A quantized build is a different model. Decision models are more sensitive to this than chat models in two ways:

* the answer is the probability distribution itself, and its calibration (ECE, Brier) can move even where the chosen
  option does not;
* AutoThink thinks when the first read-out's top probability is below 0.9. A shift of a few hundredths in that
  probability changes which questions think, and a question that thinks in one build and not in the other can end
  with a different answer, latency and token count.

Compare every build with BF16 on the same requests:

```bash
startlux-decide eval --url http://127.0.0.1:8090 --data gold.jsonl --out bf16.jsonl     # BF16 server
startlux-decide eval --url http://127.0.0.1:8091 --data gold.jsonl --out fp8.jsonl      # the build
startlux-decide eval --compare bf16.jsonl fp8.jsonl
```

`--compare` reports the agreement of the chosen answers, both accuracies and their difference with a 95% bootstrap
interval over requests, the agreement of the gate's decisions (thought or not), and the largest change of any option's
probability per question.

| model | build | engine | agreement with BF16 | accuracy BF16 â†’ build (95% CI of the difference) | thought decisions agree | max \|Î”p\| (mean) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4B Instant | FP8 | vLLM | TODO | TODO | n/a | TODO |
| 4B AutoThink | FP8 | vLLM | TODO | TODO | TODO | TODO |
| 4B AutoThink | GGUF Q8_0 | llama.cpp | TODO | TODO | TODO | TODO |
| 4B AutoThink | GGUF Q4_K_M | llama.cpp | TODO | TODO | TODO | TODO |
| 4B AutoThink | MLX 8-bit | mlx-vlm | TODO | TODO | TODO | TODO |
